question: How can density functional theory calculations be used to estimate barrier heights and effects of molecular motion on carbon-oxygen stretching frequencies?
answer: Density functional theory (DFT) calculations can estimate barrier heights and the effects of molecular motion on carbon-oxygen (C-O) stretching frequencies by modeling potential energy surfaces and vibrational modes. These calculations are essential for interpreting temperature-dependent IR spectra, particularly in metal carbonyl complexes, where torsional or rotational motion can significantly influence C-O band behavior. DFT provides quantitative insights into energy barriers and frequency shifts, helping validate or refine spectral interpretations, such as confirming fast diene rotation in [(η4-norbornadiene)Fe(CO)3]. Without DFT, distinguishing chemical exchange from other dynamic processes in IR spectra remains challenging.

### Task 1: Summarize the purpose of the paper
The purpose of the paper is to revisit and evaluate the interpretation of the temperature-dependent behavior of the low-frequency C-O bands in the IR spectrum of [(η4-norbornadiene) Fe (CO)3], originally attributed to fast rotation of the diene group by Grevels in 1987. The authors analyze previous claims and provide new insights, primarily through the application of density functional theory (DFT) calculations, to support Grevels' original interpretation.
